synopsis: Southborough boards focused heavily this week on finalizing warrant positions for the October 17 Special Town Meeting and preparing preliminary FY28 operating budgets. The Select Board and Advisory Committee took diverging positions on major warrant articles, with the Select Board endorsing two-family zoning amendments and golf course irrigation funding while the Advisory Committee voted against recommending both. At the same time, municipal departments including the Library, Board of Health, and Conservation Commission reviewed severe cut scenarios that would reduce staff hours, programming, and subscriptions if an anticipated town tax override fails next spring. In other business, the Conservation Commission asked to retain $100,000 in authorized borrowing for Breakneck Hill Farm restoration, and the Select Board awarded contracts for municipal road paving and heating oil.

highlights.title: Select Board and Advisory Committee split on Town Meeting warrant articles
highlights.why: The Select Board recommended seven of eight warrant articles, endorsing two-family zoning changes and golf course irrigation while opposing CPA funding for a trail bridge. The Advisory Committee voted against recommending the zoning revisions, golf course funding, and the trail footbridge.

highlights.title: Town departments model service and staff cuts under override-failure budget scenarios
highlights.why: Departments prepared dual FY28 budget submissions following guidance tied to an anticipated spring tax override. Modeled zero-increase scenarios would eliminate library programming and subscriptions, reduce hours for health staff, and cut 125 annual hours from the Conservation Agent position.

highlights.title: Trails Committee plans outreach after boards reject bridge funding article
highlights.why: Following votes by both the Select Board and Advisory Committee against supporting $217,318 in additional CPA money for the Peninsula Trail footbridge, the committee planned voter education and drafted a fallback request to extend the expiration of $211,000 in existing funds.

highlights.title: Conservation Commission seeks to retain $100,000 for Breakneck Hill Farm dump work
highlights.why: The commission voted 4-1 to ask the Select Board to preserve $100,000 in authorized borrowing capacity to fund habitat restoration, soil work, and trail repairs rather than rescinding the full $727,960 at Town Meeting.

highlights.title: ZBA finalizes two-family dwelling warrant article language
highlights.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved cleaned-up language for Special Town Meeting Article 2, which removes a two-year waiting period to convert single-family homes into two-family dwellings.

highlights.title: Select Board awards FY27 road paving and fuel oil contracts
highlights.why: The board awarded paving contracts across six roads after bids came in approximately $400,000 below engineering estimates, and approved a municipal heating oil contract at $2.99 per gallon.
